en.html:
That <ruby>knight<rt>Crusader</rt></ruby>.

The distinctive shape of his tsurugi stirred another memory. A Western-history reference book I had read at school.

One of its photographs. The supreme treasure of the <ruby>permanently neutral nation<rt>Schwyz</rt></ruby>—William Tell, the Saint of the Bow.

It had served that great hero of medieval Europe; after his death it was kept as a treasure bearing his name. A celebrated armor even among celebrated armors. Legend said the bolts from its left-arm <ruby>crossbow<rt>crossbow</rt></ruby> were magic missiles, certain to strike and certain to kill. It had even shot precisely through the apple upon his son’s head, they said.

That knight’s tsurugi was the very image of the sacred treasure.

But—it was not the same.

Another thing altogether.

Certainly, a national treasure could hardly be taken abroad so easily. But even without considering that, my eye had not <ruby>judged<rt>seen</rt></ruby> that tsurugi to be genuine.

A <ruby>forgery<rt>forgery</rt></ruby>.
A counterfeit.

Its shape had been stolen with remarkable skill. Very likely its armor-steel was scarcely weaker than the original’s. But something was seeping through its surface which the Saint of the Bow did not possess in the smallest degree.

The smith’s vanity.
A powerful, twisted pride.

Impersonate a famous hero’s tsurugi to steal its reputation—and still privately believe your own work the superior article. That small, warped human figure showed through.

No one looking upon that tsurugi would sigh in admiration. They would only frown and give a displeased grunt.

And it was with such a tsurugi————that my adoptive father had been killed.

ja.html:
あの<ruby>騎士<rt>クルセイダー</rt></ruby>。

　劒冑の特徴的な造形は、別の記憶を刺激する。
　昔、学校で読んだ西洋史の資料集。

　その中に掲載されていた写真の一枚。
　<ruby>永世中立国<rt>シュヴィーツ</rt></ruby>の至宝――〝弓聖〟ウィリアム・テル。

　中世欧州史を彩る偉大な英雄が愛用し、彼の死後は
その名を冠して秘蔵された、名甲中の名甲である。
　伝説に曰く、左腕の<ruby>石弓<rt>クロスボウ</rt></ruby>から放たれる矢は必中必殺
の魔弾。息子の頭上の林檎すら的確に射抜いたと云う。

　あの騎士の劒冑はその聖宝に瓜二つだ。

　しかし――違う。

　別物。

　無論、一国の国宝が容易く持ち出される筈がないと
いう判断もある。
　だがその点に思いを致さずとも、俺の眼はあの劒冑
を真物とは<ruby>鑑<rt>み</rt></ruby>なかった。

　あれは<ruby>贋作<rt>がんさく</rt></ruby>。
　紛い物だ。

　造形こそ、見事なまでに盗み取ってはいる。きっと
甲鉄の強度も真物におさおさ劣るまい。
　しかし〝弓聖〟には欠片も無いものが、その表面に
滲んで現れていた。

　鍛冶師の虚栄心。
　強烈な、けれども捻じ曲がった自負。

　名高い英雄の劒冑を騙って名声を盗むような真似を
しておきながら、その劒冑よりも自分の造った品の方
が実際は優れているのだと思い込む……
　そんな卑小な、屈折した人間像が透けているのだ。

　あの劒冑は決して見る人に感嘆の吐息をつかせる事
はない。
　眉をひそめさせ、不快げな唸りを上げさせるだけだ
ろう。

　そんな劒冑で――――養父は殺された。

Kageaki"For certain reasons, he had removed himself from the Minato family register. After that, he used Kikuchi, his former surname from before he married into the family."

Sayo"...I see."

Kageaki"Had I acted on your warning and gone there at once... I might have protected him. My adoptive father... from the arrow that knight fired..."

Kageaki"...That knight..."

ja.text:
あの弓騎士。

　あれは――あれは間違いなく進駐軍の騎士だ。

　香奈枝嬢に、奴の素性を尋ねるべきだ！
　こちらは知っているに違いない！◆


　……その考えは雷光のように閃いて、消えた。

en.html:
And once I knew, what then?
Find him, attack him, take revenge?

If I did that—where would it leave Captain Ootori?

The prisoner she had brought with her would have escaped, and used information she herself supplied to cut down a knight—a <ruby>true-forged tsurugi<rt>Blood Crux</rt></ruby> owner was almost certainly a member of the traditional aristocracy.
...No one would defend a heretic from Yamato.

This would go far beyond causing her trouble.
I could not do it.

—Nothing could be done.
Against my adoptive father’s killer, I could do nothing.

知ってどうする。
　探し出し、襲い、復讐するのか。

　そんなことをすれば――大鳥大尉の立場はどうなる。

　自分の連れてきた捕虜が脱走し、しかも自分の提供
した情報によって騎士――<ruby>真打劒冑<rt>ブラッドクルス</rt></ruby>の所有者ならまず
間違いなく伝統的貴族階級だ――を斬ったとなれば。
　……大和出身の異端者を弁護する者はいないだろう。

　迷惑で済む話ではない。
　できる筈がなかった。

　――何もできない。
　養父の仇に、俺は何もすることができない。
